title: Listen for /ʃ/, /tʃ/ and /dʒ/
goal: Hear and distinguish /ʃ/, /tʃ/ and /dʒ/ in simple word models.
cue: For sh, let the air continue. For ch, briefly stop the air before releasing into the sh-like sound. Avoid adding a separate vowel.
spelling: sh often represents /ʃ/; ch often represents /tʃ/. They are useful patterns, not rules for every word.
task: Ask whether a shop is open. Repeat the key word shop clearly.
story: A shop sells chips. Ben buys a small bag.
reviewPrompt: Return to day 16, 23, 27, 29. Recall a word or say one useful phrase before opening those lessons.

cards.title: How to make it clear
sections: For /ʃ/, keep air flowing behind the tooth ridge. For /tʃ/, briefly close then release there. /dʒ/, as in jeep, has a similar closure and release with voice. Keep the whole sound short; do not add “uh”.
Use a mirror if helpful. Keep your jaw and throat comfortable. Stop if the movement hurts; do not force it.

articulation.label: Sound /tʃ/

articulation.label: Sound /dʒ/
articulation.alt: Sound /dʒ/: /dʒ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
